title: Oscar and the Detention
premise: Sebastian Eriksen, seventeen, has spent years keeping his family afloat in the fading mill town of Halloway while his mother works nights—until his college essay prompt, 'Describe a moment you cannot forget,' unlocks memories that aren't his. He discovers the town's beloved founding tradition, the Detention (a century-old rite where seniors are 'held back' one night to confess their truths), was built on an erasure: the founders' first victim, a boy named Oscar, whose name and story were scrubbed from every record. As Sebastian digs, the town's most powerful families close ranks, because the Detention's confessional magic—the thing that made Halloway feel like home—runs on Oscar's forgotten grief. In the end, Sebastian chooses exposure over protection, restoring Oscar's memory at the cost of the tradition itself, and learns that a found family willing to remember together is stronger than any ritual.
about_author: Zephyrine Galloway is the pen name of a former night-shift librarian who grew up in a mill town much like Halloway and never stopped wondering what the plaques left out. This is their second novel for young adults, following the acclaimed 'The Quiet Year of Marisol Vane.'

chapters.title: Everything Is Fine
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. A chaotic morning—burnt toast, missing permission slips, little sister Wren's scraped knee—establishes his role as surrogate parent while Mom sleeps off her night shift. At school, the college essay prompt lands on his desk. Emotional beat: weary competence masking exhaustion; he writes 'I don't remember' as a joke and feels something answer.

chapters.title: The Question That Answers Back
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. His draft essay keeps writing itself into memories he can't place—a cold gymnasium, a boy's voice saying 'my name is Oscar.' He assumes stress. His best friend Priya notices him sleepwalking toward the old school annex. Emotional beat: uncanny dread braided with dark humor about his nonexistent free time.

chapters.title: Oscar
chapters.summary: Alternating POV begins: brief interludes in Oscar's voice, 1923, a scholarship boy wrongly accused of theft, facing the school's first 'Detention.' Sebastian finds Oscar's name scratched out of the founding ledger in the archive. Emotional beat: recognition across a century; two boys erased by duty.

chapters.title: The Tradition That Made the Town
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. He attends the Detention's centennial planning gala, where Mayor Ashford and the founding families perform nostalgia. The ritual's confessional magic is real—attendees glow with unburdened relief—but Sebastian feels it pulling at his own memories, smoothing them over. Emotional beat: seduction of belonging versus instinct that something is being taken.

chapters.title: What Wren Remembers
chapters.summary: Wren's POV, age nine. She's been drawing the same boy in her sketchbook for months and calls him 'the brother before.' Her matter-of-fact certainty cracks Sebastian open: the memory-erasure touches even the little ones he swore to protect. Emotional beat: protective guilt transformed into resolve.

chapters.title: Ashford's Bargain
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Mayor Ashford privately offers Sebastian a full ride to any college—and his mother a day job—if he stops digging before the centennial Detention. The offer is generous, kind even, which makes it worse. Emotional beat: temptation; power corrupting through generosity rather than menace.

chapters.title: The Annex at Night
chapters.summary: Sebastian, Priya, and Wren break into the sealed annex and find the original detention room preserved like a shrine: Oscar's initials, his confiscated letters, evidence that each generation's Detention has fed on a new 'forgotten one.' Oscar's interlude reveals he died there, alone, waiting to be remembered. Emotional beat: grief and fury fused into purpose.

chapters.title: Collateral
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Retaliation begins: Mom loses shifts, Priya's scholarship is threatened, Wren's sketches vanish from her backpack. Sebastian nearly accepts the bargain to protect them, but Oscar's voice reminds him that protection through forgetting is how Halloway got here. Emotional beat: the cost of truth made concrete; lowest point.

chapters.title: The Centennial Detention
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs converge. At the ritual, instead of the scripted confession, Sebastian takes the floor and speaks Oscar's name, reading his letters aloud as the room's magic turns on its keepers—every founding family forced to remember what they buried. Ashford collapses under a century of complicity; the crowd must choose. Emotional beat: cathartic climax; truth as detonation.

chapters.title: Attendance Taken
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV, weeks later. The Detention is dissolved; the town, raw but honest, votes to build a memorial with Oscar's real name restored. Sebastian's finished essay isn't about survival—it's about Oscar, and it gets him into college on its own merits. Wren draws Oscar smiling now. Emotional beat: found family holding memory together; quiet, earned hope.
